newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Hard left Russian communists come to blows.
newsitem.headline: Hard left Russian communists come to blows.

text.p: Hardline Russian leftists scuffled and fought on Saturday during the Moscow congress of a communist splinter party, shocking television viewers used to the stage-managed and unanimous communist gatherings of Soviet days.

The fisticuffs were the latest manifestation of a bitter split between Viktor Anpilov, leader of the Working Russia movement, and rivals trying to oust him from the Russian Communist Workers Party, of which Anpilov's group is a part.

As Anpilov, calling on the working class to march on Moscow armed with picks and tractors, attempted to secure the election of supporters to the central committee of Working Russia, an opponent leapt to the platform and grabbed a microphone.
The man was bundled off struggling, sparking scuffles in the hall and a barrage of abuse from rival groups.

Anpilov was sacked as RCWP central committee secretary in July, charged with "radicalism". A television commentator said some of his rivals accused him of "petty bourgeois tendencies" and were trying to oust him from Working Russia too.

The RCWP fell just short of the five percent of the vote needed to win seats in parliament in last December's election. It supported mainstream communist Gennady Zyuganov in his bid for the presidency in July but has criticised his moderation.
Anpilov, a journalist and fiery speaker in the Bolshevik mode, wants to restore the Soviet Union.
